requirement: Serve reusable MCP prompts whose FastMCP-like argument declarations are checked against the template and every render request.
skeleton: A PromptError, frozen PromptArgument and Message dataclasses, and a Prompt that validates its role and template fields, describes its arguments and renders with defaults.
caption: FastMCP-style prompt templates written in the standard library with string.Formatter and dataclasses and no third-party imports. PromptError covers declaration and render problems. PromptArgument is a frozen dataclass with name, required and default, and Message holds role and content. Prompt raises PromptError for a role other than user or assistant and for any template field, including a positional one, that is not a declared argument. describe lists names and required flags. render raises PromptError for unknown or missing required values, fills optional ones from their defaults and formats once with format_map, so braces inside values stay literal. The fixture asserts values and defaults, empty optional defaults, literal braces, the unknown, missing, undeclared and role errors, and describe.

constraints: Roles other than user or assistant raise PromptError
Template fields that are not declared arguments raise PromptError
Unknown or missing required render values raise PromptError
Optional arguments fall back to their declared default
Values are substituted once so their braces stay literal

rationale.teaches: Check the template against the declared arguments at definition time and the request against them at render time.
rationale.why: Prompt arguments come from MCP clients, so undeclared fields and unchecked values surface as KeyErrors or silently wrong prompts.

ops.docstring: FastMCP-style prompts whose declared arguments render into messages.

ops.source:
class PromptError(Exception):
    """Raised for badly declared prompts and bad render arguments."""

candidates.why_wrong: A template naming an undeclared field is accepted and fails later with KeyError.
Misspelled render arguments are silently ignored instead of rejected.
Optional arguments are demanded as if they were required.
Declared defaults are ignored and optional fields render empty.
An unsupported system role is accepted for the rendered message.
